title: Bounded rewind to the initial input position
statement: Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S$ be a state type, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine with states in $S$. Choose states $a,b\in S$ and a possible destination $d\in\mathrm{Option}(S)$. Suppose that in state $a$, for every scanned input and work-tape symbols, the transition is the control action that moves the input head left and enters state $b$. Suppose also that in state $b$, it moves left and stays in $b$ when the scanned input symbol is present, and moves left and enters $d$ when that symbol is absent; in both cases these are control actions. If a configuration $c$ on input $x$ has state $a$, then there is a number of steps $t\le c$'s input-head position $+2$ after which the machine's configuration has state $d$ and input-head position $1$, with all other components equal to those of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a $k$-work-tape Turing machine over Boolean symbols with states in $S$
From state $a$, for every input and work-tape reading, the transition is the left-moving control action entering $b$
From state $b$, on a present input symbol, the transition is the left-moving control action staying in $b$
From state $b$, on an absent input symbol, the transition is the left-moving control action entering $d$
$c$ is a configuration on input $x$ with state $a$
